review_notes: I read the whole file and grepped Mathlib for "empiricalMeasure", "empirical measure" and "Krylov". Every hit was in the target file, so I found no existing empirical-measure or Krylov–Bogolyubov development to compete with. `empiricalMeasure` is defined directly as `birkhoffAverage NNReal f Measure.dirac (n + 1) x`, so it reuses Mathlib's Birkhoff average, and its integral lemmas go through `integral_birkhoffAverage_measure` and `birkhoffAverage_comp_apply`. It is a named specialisation, not a rival concept. The probability-measure instance and the use of `ProbabilityMeasure`, `MapClusterPt`, `MeasurePreserving` and `Measure.Regular` all build on existing Mathlib notions. I did not search exhaustively for other Dirac-average constructions elsewhere, so there is some residual uncertainty. I have no concrete evidence of a duplicate.
